To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
RSG 2.2 binds more specifically and tightly to RRE than Rev because it uses more base-specific contacts and a stronger salt bridge network to hold it in place.
the Rev peptide binds to the RRE RNA through a combination of shape recognition, base-specific hydrogen bonding, and cation pi interactions.
RSG 2.1 and Rev bind RRE stem IIA differently, and that RSG 3.1 and Rev both bind RRE stem IIIB differently.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding on an atomic level the structural and dynamic properties of two arginine-rich peptide-RNA complexes.
understanding how two arginine rich peptides, of similar length and sequence but with grossly different secondary structure, recognize the same sequence in RNA with such different binding modes.
understanding on an atomic level the molecular recognition of a viral RNA by two peptides of similar sequence and length but very different structural conformations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
RSG  1.2 is a better RNA-binding peptide because of a combination of shape recognition and salt bridge interactions that hold the peptide in place.
the two peptides recognize the RRE sequence through similar interactions, but the Rev peptide recognizes the RNA in a more flexible and dynamic manner than RSG 1.

the Rev peptide binds to the RRE stem IIA and stem IIB regions through shape recognition and cation-pii interactions, whereas RSG 1-2 binds to the same regions through base-specific hydrogen bonding, water-mediated hydrogen bonding, shape recognition, cation-pii and cation-ii interactions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
water, shape recognition, and salt bridges are important in stabilizing the Rev peptide-RNA complex, while cation-pi and base-specific interactions are more important in stabilizing RSG 1-2-RNA.
RSG 2.0 is an excellent mimic of Rev for RRE binding and that it is a good model for the Rev-RRE interaction.
the RSG 1 peptide is a more efficient RNA-binding agent than Rev because of its greater affinity and higher specificity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the RSG 1-2 peptide binds to the same RNA sequence as the Rev peptide, but uses different strategies to do so.
RSG 2.2 binds more strongly to the RRE than the wild-type peptide by forming a more extensive set of contacts with the RNA and by using water molecules to mediate peptide/RNA interactions.
RSG 2.1 binds to RRE with a much more favorable binding affinity than the wild-type Rev peptide.
